title: am
intro:
The ’am’ component describes various kinds of fertilizer and other added matter
such as crop residues. In particular, it describes how they decompose.

sections.name: base
sections.desc: Common attributes for all added organic matter models.
sections.sig:
< base (name name )
          (initialized false)
          (creation creation )
          (lock lock )
          (om om ...) >

attrs.name: name
attrs.doc: A name given to this AOM so you can identify it in for example log files.

attrs.name: initialized
attrs.doc:
True if this AM has been initialized. It will usually be false in user setup files,
     but true in checkpoints.

attrs.name: creation
attrs.doc:
Optional submodel
     Time this AM was created.

attrs.name: lock
attrs.doc:
Optional submodel
     This AM belongs to a still living plant
        < (crop crop )
             (part part ) >

attrs.name: – crop
attrs.doc: Crop to which this am is locked

attrs.name: – part
attrs.doc: Crop part to which this am is locked

attrs.name: om
attrs.doc:
Optional component
     The individual AOM pools.

sections.name: initial
sections.desc:
A ‘base’ model (see 17.1, page 103) build into Daisy.
   Initial added organic matter at the start of the simulation.
sections.sig:
< initial (layers layers ...)
                 ;; Shared parameters are described in section 17.1.
                 (name name )
                 (initialized false)
                 (creation creation )
                 (lock lock )
                 (om om ...) >

attrs.name: layers
attrs.doc:
Carbon content in different soil layers. The carbon is assumed to be uniformly
        distributed in each layer.
          <    end weight     >
          – end : number [cm]
            Parameter
            Height where this layer ends (a negative number).
          – weight: number [kg C/m2 ]
            Parameter
            Carbon in this layer.

sections.name: organic
sections.desc:
A ‘base’ model (see 17.1, page 103) build into Daisy.
   Organic fertilizer, typically slurry or manure from animals.
sections.sig:
< organic (weight 0 [Mg w.w./ha])
                 (total C fraction total C fraction )
                 (total N fraction total N fraction )
                 (NH4 fraction 0 [<fraction>])
                 (volatilization 0 [<fraction>])
                 (first year utilization first year utilization )
                 (second year utilization second year utilization )
                 (dry matter fraction dry matter fraction )
                 (NO3 fraction 0 [<fraction>])
                 ;; Shared parameters are described in section 17.1.
                 (name name )
                 (initialized false)
                 (creation creation )
                 (lock lock )
                 (om om ...) >

attrs.name: weight
attrs.doc: Amount of fertilizer applied.

attrs.name: total C fraction
attrs.doc: Carbon fraction of dry matter.

attrs.name: total N fraction
attrs.doc: Nitrogen fraction of dry matter.

attrs.name: NH4 fraction
attrs.doc:
Ammonium fraction of total N in fertilizer. The remaining nitrogen is assumed
     to be nitrate or organic.

attrs.name: volatilization
attrs.doc: Fraction of NH4 that evaporates on application.

attrs.name: first year utilization
attrs.doc:
Estimated useful N fraction for the first year. In Denmark, this is governed
     by legalisation.

attrs.name: second year utilization
attrs.doc:
Estimated useful N fraction for the second year. In Denmark, this is governed
     by legalisation.

attrs.name: dry matter fraction
attrs.doc: Dry matter fraction of total (wet) weight.

attrs.name: NO3 fraction
attrs.doc:
Nitrate fraction of total N in fertilizer. The remaining nitrogen is assumed to
     be ammonium or organic.

sections.name: root
sections.desc:
A ‘base’ model (see 17.1, page 103) build into Daisy.
   Initialization of old root remains.
sections.sig:
< root (depth depth )
              (om om ...)                             ; Has default value.
              (dist 7 [cm])
              (weight 1.2 [Mg DM/ha])
              (total C fraction 0.4 [<fraction>])
              (total N fraction 0.01 [<fraction>])
              ;; Shared parameters are described in section 17.1.
              (name name )
              (initialized false)
              (creation creation )
              (lock lock ) >

attrs.name: depth
attrs.doc:
How far down does the old root reach? (a negative number) By default, the
     soils maximal rooting depth will be used.

attrs.name: dist
attrs.doc: Distance to go down in order to decrease the root density to half the original.

attrs.name: weight
attrs.doc: Total weight of old root dry matter.

attrs.name: total C fraction
attrs.doc: Carbon fraction of total root dry matter

attrs.name: total N fraction
attrs.doc: Nitrogen fraction of total root dry matter

sections.text:

    depth: number [cm]

     soils maximal rooting depth will be used.
    dist: number [cm]
     Parameter (default 7)
     Distance to go down in order to decrease the root density to half the original.
    weight: number [Mg DM/ha]
     Parameter (default 1.2)
     Total weight of old root dry matter.

       total C fraction: number [<fraction>]
        Parameter (default 0.4)
        Carbon fraction of total root dry matter

sections.name: state
sections.desc:
A ‘base’ model (see 17.1, page 103) build into Daisy.
    Most AM models are only used for initialization, they will be comnverted to
this generic model after creation, so this is what you will see in a checkpoint. This
model contains a number (typically 2) of separate pools, each of which have their
own turnover rate.
